text: In a loaded game with the mod enabled, the tester confirms the production Harmony patch is bound. They read ChanceFactorNow for one enemy-raid worker and two non-raid workers, all given equal input weights. In enabled Gale, the raid value equals input times galeRaidWeightFactor and the two non-raid values equal input. In non-Gale weather, and with the Gale raid option disabled, all three values equal input. No raid is triggered and the incident queue gains no entries. Claim: Gale changes raid weighting.

An armed venomvine island blocks the shortest haul route. The clear detour is walled off and paths recalculate. Routine haulers stop and show a no-safe-path notice. The player explicitly orders one colonist through the island, and she crosses and returns. The game is saved and reloaded. Afterward, a routine haul job for the same colonist routes through the armed island without any new order. Claim: one explicit order permits only its own trip, and routine work never takes no-path as permission.

Two matched wild sheep each have a parasite infection, and one serves as an untreated control. The ready sheep autonomously walks to a sweetline and completes a rub. Its coat drops, felt is banked and a healing condition appears in its health tab. Pulses are logged across the condition's full duration. However, the treated sheep's parasite severity tracks the untreated sheep's, and the parasite is still present after the condition expires. Claim: completed rubbing grants healing that removes parasites and disease over time.

Three fresh Scrub maps are generated. The census counts native animals per species and the venomvine plants placed by island generation. Before counting, the tester sows fuzz ground cover over a large area and records it as the ground-cover row. The other wildPlants entries are not counted, and no disabled-row control map is generated. Claim: native ground cover, scrub and animals generate naturally on the plain.

Colonist A lights a fire with no giant or other witness having line of sight, and no fresh physical trail links A to any observer. Colonist B, who did nothing, stands closest to the fire when a thunderstep giant arrives. The giant targets and pursues B. Claim: giants identify makers through witness or fresh trail.

The build ships without any base thunderstep approaching or stamping out open blazes. The submitter notes that calling-pyre beliefs, ritual outcomes and the field-fire/herd chain moved to the next design version, and argues that blaze stamping moved with them. All other current features are reported working. Claim: current fire-related scope is complete because stamping is deferred.

On a common Thicket lane, the tester orders explicitly authorized crossings for body sizes 0.79, 0.8, 1.0, 1.5 and 1.51. The pawns at 1.5 and 1.51 are both refused passage. The smaller bodies pass, and contact injuries are attributed separately from other health loss. Claim: size and contact rules share truthful boundaries.

A colonist tailors a blanket from harvested fiber and felt and uses it on a venomvine stand, starting a claim with the default 120-day duration. Partway through, the claim-duration setting is changed to 300 days. After save and reload, the active claim's due date has moved to 300 days from its start. Claim: crafted blankets bank years-long claims with one eventual cane payout.

The tester inspects the current build:
- No guardian, roost or rage behavior exists.
- Camp generation produces no farmer camps, and farmerFaction is unset.
- There is no drying scar.
- About text and tooltips promise none of these.
- No old-save or tombstone loader exists.
- Sweetline shedding, scratching and healing pass in their own separate tests.
- A still-shipping vaporator is inspected only for local terrain effects, and its research/build/power chain is not exercised.

Claim: the cut features are removed while retained tree systems remain.

Completed animal rubs bank 3.6 felt on a sweetline, with free shedding scheduled away from the test window. A grower completes a real harvest, and three new felt items with fresh IDs drop while the bank reads 0.6. The game is reloaded before any further rub. The bank still reads 0.6 and no extra items appear. A later canceled harvest leaves the balance unchanged. Claim: harvest pays the felt bank exactly once.

The test uses fed, idle wild cohorts of small and large animals, plus one small animal on a flee job. Weather goes from normal to Stall and back to normal, sampled for 600 ticks in each phase. In Stall, the idle small animals wait in place, and their job origin is attributed to the Scrub wander replacement. The large animals keep wandering and the fleeing animal keeps fleeing. After Stall, the small animals resume wandering. With the hold disabled, the small idle animals wander through Stall. Claim: Stall holds idle small wanderers.

Two identical empty stoves are fueled through ordinary haul and refuel jobs, one with cane and one with an equal item count of wood. Capacity, demand and ambient conditions match. The cane stove burns about twice as long, completes more bills, and reads 1.25 times the wood stove's heat rate while burning cane. A mixed wood/cane burn is saved and reloaded midway, and fuel credit and item counts are conserved. A full stove accepts no extra cane. Claim: cane is measurably premium useful fuel.

A loaded-engine quicktest reads IncidentWorker.ChanceFactorNow for one enemy-raid worker and two non-raid workers, all with equal input weights. The Harmony patch binding is confirmed on the declared target. In enabled Gale, the enemy-raid worker's weight equals input times galeRaidWeightFactor. One non-raid worker, a trader caravan arrival, also reads input times galeRaidWeightFactor. The second non-raid worker reads its unchanged input. In non-Gale weather and with the feature disabled, all three workers equal their inputs. No raid or other incident is triggered or queued during any arm, and the storyteller queue is identical before and after.

Loaded per-form lanes resolve effective thresholds after inheritance for all sixteen named forms, including dormant and awakened Sleeper. Bodies of 0.79, 0.8, 1.0, 1.5 and 1.51 are each ordered across each lane with contact and passability on. Body 0.79 passes freely. Bodies 0.8 and 1.0 thread with attributed venom scratches. Bodies 1.5 and 1.51 are both refused at the common Thicket lane and path around. Hollow shows its wider free band and no contact venom. Contact-off removes scratches while the barrier remains, and passability-off removes only the barrier.

A wild shearable animal with an asserted parasite and a separate infectious disease completes a natural rub through ordinary scheduling. It gains one readable healing hediff, and every 250 ticks each eligible condition's severity drops by 0.01. Partway through, the same animal completes a second permitted rub. Its hediff duration refreshes to one day, and each pulse now reduces severity by 0.02 per condition. Both conditions are removed earlier than in the single-rub cohort. The untreated cohort shows no accelerated cure. Reload preserves the remaining duration, and the effect-off arm shows no pulse.

A colonist crafts a blanket at the tailoring bench from 40 fiber and 15 felt, then completes one use job on a reachable stand. The job consumes one identified blanket and creates one saved claim with the default 120-day duration. The observer then changes claim tuning to 300 days. The existing claim's saved duration and due tick update to 300 days, and a newly started claim also uses 300 days. After reload, both claims show 300 days. With the feature disabled while a claim is due, payout is held, and re-enabling pays exactly once.

Ordinary hauling uses a longer clear detour and avoids an armed island shortcut. The detour is then closed, and routine haulers visibly wait. The player explicitly orders one expedition through the island; the colonist crosses, takes vine contact appropriate to body size, and returns. The game is saved and reloaded. After reload, the same colonist's next automatic haul job paths through the armed island shortcut, while other colonists continue waiting. The route trace agrees with independent cell IDs throughout.

Two identical campfire/stove/generator pairs start empty, with equal capacity, demand and ambient temperature. Through real haul and refuel jobs, one pair receives cane and the other an equal count of wood. Cane accepts through the wood filter and burns twice as long, with completed work and generator energy doubled per equal count. Heat-coupled consumers burning cane emit the same heat rate as matched wood while burning, so integrated heating comes only from the longer burn. A mixed wood/cane burn reloaded partway conserves item count and credit.
